evidence.quote: Earth observation satellite – specifically for coral reef and ocean monitoring
only one satellite is required. This also just allows for simplicity
would likely be used by governmental and science agencies (e.g. CSIRO, BOM)

criteria.reasoning: Primary mission (coral reef fluid lensing), rationale (bleaching, acidification), single-sat justification, and users (CSIRO/BOM, Aus Gov/university) all explained with references. Could be more detailed on customers vs operator but meets all 4 points.

evidence.quote: The proposed satellite will thus use the Vega E rocket as a launch vehicle – launched from the Guiana Space Centre Spaceport.
altitude of 600km requires a mean inclination of 97.7924° for the satellite to remain sun-synchronous.
Average contact duration of almost ten minutes was achieved, in addition to the already frequent amount of passes.

criteria.reasoning: Launch site/vehicle justified with trade analysis, SSO LEO defined with altitude, inclination, a, e, RAAN, argument of latitude, STK screenshots Images 1-5; ground station Mt Pleasant with access report and communication stats; duration 5yr and drag-sail EOL covered. Strong evidence, minor simplification of J2.

evidence.quote: A polar sun-synchronous orbit allows for consistent illumination of the oceans while maintaining a constant sun angle.
Mt Pleasant Radio Observatory is well-located to receive data from this orbit type constantly

criteria.reasoning: Conclusion synthesizes launch, SSO orbit, ground contact and EOL, links back to bleaching problem, notes Vega E risk and alternative Vega C. Appropriate and detailed from body evidence.

evidence.quote: This report outlines the intended designs and procedures involved in the construction of a Earth observation satellite

criteria.reasoning: Report has required sections and STK tables/figures, but figure captions inconsistent, some OCR table artefacts, grammar flaws, and uses Wikipedia despite prohibition, with inconsistent referencing style. Readable but not fully professional.

technical_issues.issue: Describes SSO maintenance as J2 perturbation causing RAAN precession of 1 deg/day, but imprecise phrasing; inclination vs altitude calc shown as Image 3 without derivation.
Uses argument of latitude u in COE table to handle circular orbit, but lists RAAN 27.33 deg as launch site location without stating LTAN/ LTDN.
Access report duplicates entry 14-15 same timestamp indicating STK export error; mean duration calculated but contact analysis does not link to Great Barrier Reef imaging windows.

overall: Solid SSO coral-reef mission with consistent launch/orbit/ground analysis and STK evidence. Good intro and conclusion. Presentation weakened by Wikipedia citation and figure labelling. EOL drag-sail appropriate for no-propulsion CubeSat class.
